title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
slides: Why is The New York Times warning photographers about Photoshop?
A new update adds AI features that scan your images
The AI can train on your photos without clear consent
Check your settings before updating to protect your work
Delay the update until you review the terms
thread_text:
1. NYT vs. Photoshop

A new update lets Adobe's AI scan your images and train on them — and photographers are being warned before they hit install.

2. The Consent Problem

Adobe's terms don't make it obvious you're opting in. Unless you dig into settings, your portfolio becomes training data.

3. Your Portfolio Is Data

Every edited photo, every client shoot, every personal project — all of it can feed a model you never agreed to build.

4. Check Before You Click

The update prompt is your last checkpoint. Open Preferences and look for the AI training toggle before it's too late.

5. Hold Off. Read First.

Delay the update until you've reviewed the new terms line by line. Would you hand over your archive without reading the fine print?
